trial_court: Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate(M), Bilasipara, Misc. Case No. 244/2017
case_name: Tarun Chandra Das vs Bhanjana Kalita
facts_of_case: The respondent is the wife of the petitioner. Their marriage was solemnised on 28.04.2017. The petitioner took the respondent to his own house at Arearjhar after two months of living together as husband and wife, where she found his first wife. The respondent claimed maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage with a person having a living spouse is not permissible and the same is void and not voidable.
legal_principles.held: As per Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, a marriage with a person having a living spouse is not permissible and the same is void and not voidable.

legal_principles.principle: The burden is always on the person who claims herself to be the legally married wife of the person from whom she claims maintenance.
legal_principles.held: And in the case in hand, the respondent has miserably failed to prove that she is legally married with the petitioner and the same fulfill the condition for a Hindu marriage as laid down in Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A woman in accordance with Hindu rights with a man having a living spouse is a complete nullity in the eye of law.
legal_principles.held: (ii). That, the marriage of a woman in accordance with Hindu rights with a man having a living spouse is a complete nullity in the eye of law and therefore, she is not entitled to the benefit of Section 125 Cr.P.C.

legal_principles.principle: To be entitled for maintenance under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C., a person must prove that she is legally married with the petitioner and fulfill the condition for a Hindu marriage as laid down in Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
legal_principles.held: (v). That, to be entitled for maintenance under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C., the burden is always on the person who claims herself to be the legally married wife of the person from whom she claims maintenance. And in the case in hand, the respondent has miserably failed to prove that she is legally married with the petitioner and the same fulfill the condition for a Hindu marriage as laid down in Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

outcome.final_order: The learned Additional District Judge, Bilasipara has affirmed the judgment and order dated 04.10.2019 passed in Misc. Case No. 244/2017 granting maintenance to the respondent.
